title: 禪宗頌古聯珠通集 (Anthology of Chan Verse Commentaries on Koans, 40 juan)
shelf_note: The Chanzong songgu lianzhu tongji, compiled by Faying and continued by Puhui. A core Chan gong'an and verse-commentary anthology. The images are a Wanli-era woodblock edition (the colophon on p.836 is dated 萬曆丁酉, i.e. 1597).
structure_note: Each image is a two-leaf spread, and the woodblock leaf numbers restart with each juan. That explains most of the 67 printed backsteps and 165 repeats; they do not point to a broken sequence. On p.836 juan 35 ends and juan 36 begins, in order. 956 records, 952 with OCR, and 950 translated per the counts (938 per the books field). The two translated counts disagree slightly.

reader_summary: This is the Song–Yuan anthology of verse comments on Chan gong'an, in a 1597 Wanli woodblock edition. The transcription is of the right text and mostly accurate, but it misreads characters that change meaning, misplaces verse attributions, and on one page drops the colophon. The English follows the sense of the koans and verses, but warn that some individual verses are garbled and some glosses (lineage names, place names) are wrong.
book_verdict: A correct, important edition with usable but uneven OCR and translation. Character misreads change the sense of individual lines (beak/back, said/day), attributions are misplaced on p.543, and the 1597 colophon is silently omitted on p.836.

title: 石門文字禪·卷二十九~卷三十 (vol 11)
shelf_note: Juefan Huihong's (德洪) Shimen wenzi Chan, the literary collection of a Northern Song Chan monk: letters, stupa inscriptions and sacrificial texts. It is Chan literature, not doctrine, but it belongs on this shelf. The images are the Siku quanshu (欽定四庫全書) manuscript copy, consistent with the 1773 date.
structure_note: Single-leaf images of the Siku quanshu copy. Juan 29 on p.26 and juan 30 on p.94 are in order. The 8 printed backsteps and 13 repeats most likely come from leaf numbers restarting per juan and from per-piece numbering. Collection 'universallibrary' is a generic IA tag. 122 pages, 120 translated.

reader_summary: This is the Siku quanshu manuscript copy of juan 29–30 of Huihong's Shimen wenzi Chan: letters, a stupa inscription for a Chan master, and sacrificial texts. The transcription is of the right text and is close on most pages, but on one sampled page it silently skips two lines, and the English then puts words in the wrong mouth. Where the OCR is complete, the English is accurate and readable.
book_verdict: A good Siku copy with mostly accurate reading and translation. One silent omission on p.45 changes who says what, so it needs a caveat.

title: Jikji (직지심체요절, Anthology of Great Buddhist Priests' Zen Teachings)
shelf_note: Baegun's Jikji simche yojeol, the 1377 Heungdeok-sa metal-type print (BnF, Gallica). A Korean Seon anthology of Chan sayings, so it belongs squarely on this shelf.
structure_note: 86 records. The last record (p.86) is the fore-edge of the volume, not a text leaf, and is catalogued as a 'spine'. Low printed-number counts are expected. 82 of 86 translated. Nothing else stands out.

reader_summary: This is the surviving second volume of the 1377 Jikji, the Goryeo metal-type anthology of Chan sayings, from the BnF scan. The transcription is of the right text and mostly accurate, but on one sampled page it drops a line of Dongshan's well-known verse. The English is generally faithful, with some misread exchanges. The closing fore-edge image is mislabelled as a 'manuscript' spine with an invented title.
book_verdict: A flagship object on this shelf with mostly good reading. A dropped verse line, a garbled Xuefeng/Yantou exchange, and the 'manuscript' label on a metal-type print would all be noticed by a Seon scholar.

title: 六祖大師法寶壇經 (Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch)
shelf_note: The Zongbao (Yuan) recension of the Platform Sutra, a core Chan text.
structure_note: 44 pages, all with OCR and translation. A modern reprint with no page numbers, so the low printed-number count is expected. 'published: Unknown'. The book is a modern typeset reprint rather than a historical witness, which matters for a scholar looking for originals.

tr_errors.english: <note>…a historical attempt to steal the Sixth Patriarch's head by a monk hired by a rival school…</note>
tr_errors.problem: invented gloss. In the tradition the would-be thief, Zhang Jingman, was hired by a Silla monk (Kim Daebi) who wanted the head for worship, not by a rival school

tr_errors.problem: 'beyond count' is completed from the next page

reader_summary: This is the standard Zongbao text of the Platform Sutra, in a modern computer-typeset reprint rather than a historical print. The transcription is near-perfect, and the English is accurate, fluent and can be trusted for the sense, apart from an occasional invented explanatory note. A scholar will ask why a modern digital reprint stands in for a historical edition.
book_verdict: The best reading quality on this shelf, with near-perfect OCR and a faithful translation. But the object is an undated modern typeset reprint, and one note invents history, so it should be shown as a reading text, not as a primary-source witness.
